orchestrator.title: Orchestrator

start.title: What should we plan?
start.description: The Orchestrator reads the project and acts through Orchester with your project's permissions: it creates tasks, starts and continues runs, and answers agents when you let it.

composer.notSetUp: The Orchestrator can't answer yet: choose a Claude Code or Codex connection and a model for it.
composer.readable: Conversations stay readable; you can send once it is set up.
composer.sendEmpty: Write a message or attach a file first.
composer.notReady: Choose and publish what the Orchestrator runs on in its settings first.
composer.afterAnswerDetail: Waits until the Orchestrator finishes this answer, then goes as the next message
composer.nowDetail: The Orchestrator gets it at its next tool call, inside this answer
composer.stopAndSendDetail: Stops this answer, then sends it as the next message

runsOn.tip: Acts with your project permissions: every action it takes is checked like the same action in the app.
runsOn.signedOut: Not signed in · sign in in Connections
runsOn.sentTo: Prompts, repository content and command output go to {{host}} under its terms. Orchester reads no plan limits there.
runsOn.publishNote: Publishes v{{version}} of the Orchestrator's settings: the next answer runs on it.
runsOn.publishOverDraft: Publishes v{{version}} and replaces the draft saved in Orchestrator settings.
runsOn.newSession: Another account starts a new session: earlier messages aren't remembered.

suggestions.plan: Plan work from a scope file: tasks with briefs and acceptance criteria.
suggestions.running: What's running, what's waiting and what's blocked right now?
suggestions.order: Suggest an order for the Todo tasks and which can run in parallel.
suggestions.idea: Talk through an idea before it becomes a task.

delivery.queuedNext: Queued · sent next, once this answer stops
delivery.notTaken: Not taken mid-answer · sent after this answer

orchestrator.stopNote: Stop ends this answer only. Tasks, runs and the queue are not touched.

stopped.nothing: Response stopped by you · {{time}} · nothing was created or changed
stopped.acted: Response stopped by you · {{time}} · what it did before stays

orchestrator.interrupted: The answer was cut short when Orchester or its runner closed
orchestrator.askAgainNote: Sends your last message once more.

failure.notSignedIn: The connection's CLI isn't signed in on this computer. Your message and this conversation are kept; nothing else changed.
failure.cannotStart: The connection's CLI couldn't be started; the runner's log says why. Your message and this conversation are kept; nothing else changed.
failure.connectionGone: The Orchestrator's connection is gone or can't run it. Choose another in Orchestrator settings; this conversation is kept.
failure.accountNone: The connection has no account to sign in with; pick another account. Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.accountFolderMissing: The account's folder {{folder}} is gone; pick another account. Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.accountUnsupported: This connection's account can't be used on this computer yet; pick another account. Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.failedBody: {{reason}} · Your message and this conversation are kept.
failure.earlierNotSignedIn: This answer failed: the CLI wasn't signed in
failure.earlierUnreachable: This answer failed: the Orchestrator couldn't start
failure.timeLimit: It ran longer than {{minutes}} minutes, the most one answer may take, and was ended. What it did until then stays; ask again in smaller parts.
failure.earlierTimeLimit: This answer was ended after {{minutes}} minutes

sendProblem.body: Your draft is kept. Retry sends it once; it is never stored twice.

orchestrator.setupFailed: What the Orchestrator runs on couldn't be read

loading.title: Loading conversation…
loading.note: Messages load together. Suggestions don't show while loading.

notFound.title: This conversation isn't in {{project}}
notFound.body: It may have been removed with its project data. Start a new conversation or open one from History.

duplicatePipeline.done: Copied a pipeline as a draft

newSession.connection: The Orchestrator runs on another connection now: this answer starts a new session and doesn't remember the earlier messages.
newSession.account: The Orchestrator's connection is on another account now: this answer starts a new session and doesn't remember the earlier messages.

what.question: {{agent}} asks a question
what.messageAnyone: An agent waits for a reply
what.planAnyone: A plan waits for a decision

wait.effectAnswering: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on, so the Orchestrator reads what the agent asked and answers it, or tells you what it asks with its recommendation.
wait.effectQueued: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on: the Orchestrator reads it after the turn under way ends, while it still waits.
wait.effectOwn: The agent asks again after the Orchestrator's own answer, so it waits for you: the Orchestrator doesn't answer it by itself.
wait.effectWaits: It waits for you on its card. Ask the Orchestrator here to read it, or answer it on the task's Conversation.
wait.effectPlan: Deciding a plan is yours, on its card. Ask the Orchestrator here to read it with you.
wait.effectPlanRead: Deciding a plan is yours, on its card. The Orchestrator reads it and tells you what it proposes.

held.projectEffect: No waiting task in {{project}} starts until you resume. Running tasks keep running.
held.groupTitle: New starts held · the group of {{task}}
held.groupEffect: No waiting task in this group starts until you resume. Running tasks keep running.
held.checked: Same action as Pause scheduling in the queue, checked against your permissions in {{project}}.

proposal.title: Start {{task}} on {{pipeline}}?
proposal.briefCut: This is only the opening of the brief: open {{task}} to read all of it before you start.
proposal.personOnly: Only a person starts a run the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.

historyPanel.empty: No conversation yet. Your first message starts one.
historyPanel.noMatch: No conversation's title has these words.
historyPanel.note: Conversations stay in this project on this computer.

settings.description: Plans work with you, drafts tasks and coordinates {{project}}'s queue.

publish.firstNote: The project chat can send once v1 is published.
publish.needsConnection: Publishing needs a connection that can run the Orchestrator.
publish.needsModel: Publishing needs a model: choose one, or type an id the connection accepts.

tabs.notBuilt: These settings aren't built yet: the Orchestrator acts with the project's permissions, reads the repository and keeps every conversation.

connection.label: Project connection
connection.description: The agent CLI and sign-in the Orchestrator runs on.

model.label: Model
model.description: From the connection's list, or Other model id… for one that isn't listed.
model.otherHint: Enter an id the connection accepts
model.invalid: A model id has no spaces and is at most {{max}} characters long.

effort.label: Reasoning effort
effort.description: CLI default leaves it to the connection's own setting.
effort.unchecked: Not checked for this model: the connection lists no efforts for it, so these are its other models'.

settings.note: A reply already under way finishes on the version it started with; a published change applies from the next reply.
settings.limits: Its tokens count toward {{project}}'s daily budget; it takes no agent slot. One answer ends after {{turns}} steps or {{minutes}} minutes.

noConnection.title: No connection in {{project}} can run the Orchestrator
noConnection.body: It needs an agent connection that answers and is signed in. Conversations stay readable; new messages can't be sent until one works.

change.approvedInChat: You approved it in the chat: “{{words}}”

personOnly.publish: Only a person publishes a draft the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.cancel: Only a person cancels a run the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.merge: Only a person merges a run the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.answer: Only a person sends an answer the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.message: Only a person sends a message the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.continue: Only a person decides how a run goes on that the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.pause: Only a person pauses a run the Orchestrator proposed to pause: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.resume: Only a person resumes a run the Orchestrator proposed to resume: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.release: Only a person releases new starts the Orchestrator proposed to release: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.repository: Only a person makes the git repository the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.git: Only a person runs a git operation the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.
personOnly.mcp: Only a person applies a change to an MCP server the Orchestrator proposed: input from automation is refused here.

mcp.effectWaitsWidens: Nothing is changed yet. Agents of the profiles that choose this server get it as shown above from their next start; agents at work keep what they started with.
mcp.effectWaits: Nothing is changed yet. Agents of the profiles that choose this server work as shown above from their next start; agents at work keep what they started with.
mcp.effectApplied: You applied it: agents that start from now on get the server as shown above.
mcp.effectDone: The Orchestrator made it itself: it widens nothing, and Let automation change agent permissions is on.
mcp.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. The MCP server stays as it was.
mcp.widens: This widens what agents may do: they run its program or reach its address, with what it is sent. Check where the program or URL came from before you apply it.
mcp.notFound: {{program}} is not found on this computer's search path or at that path: applying it is refused until it is installed or the path is right.
mcp.callsAsk: Every call asks, for profiles that ask before MCP actions
mcp.callsRun: {{tools}} run without asking; every other call asks

repository.waitsCommit: Make the first commit of {{project}}'s repository?
repository.doneCommit: Made the first commit of {{project}}'s repository
repository.effectWaits: Nothing is made yet. git init runs in the project's folder, then the first commit is made by the author git is set up with. No remote is added, nothing is pushed and git's settings stay as they are.
repository.effectWaitsCommit: Nothing is committed yet. The first commit is made by the author git is set up with; the repository's history stays untouched otherwise. No remote is added, nothing is pushed and git's settings stay as they are.
repository.effectApplied: The folder is a git repository on {{branch}} with its first commit: runs can branch from it now.
repository.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was made in the folder.
repository.noGitignore: No .gitignore: every file of the folder is committed
repository.gitignoreKept: .gitignore · the folder's own, kept as it is
repository.sensitive: These files look as if they hold secrets and would be committed: {{files}}. Applying it commits them; if they should stay out, dismiss it and ask for a .gitignore that keeps them out.
repository.sensitiveMore: These files look as if they hold secrets and would be committed: {{files}} and {{more}} more. Applying it commits them; if they should stay out, dismiss it and ask for a .gitignore that keeps them out.

answer.waits: Answer the question in run #{{run}} of {{task}}?
answer.done: Answered the question in run #{{run}} of {{task}}
answer.refused: Answer to run #{{run}} of {{task}} · not done
answer.effectWaits: Nothing is sent yet. Send answer gives the asking agent this answer: {{answer}}. The task's conversation shows it as the Orchestrator's.
answer.effectSent: The agent got this answer at {{time}}: {{answer}}. The task's conversation shows it as the Orchestrator's.
answer.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was sent; the agent still waits for an answer.

message.waits: Send a message to the agents of run #{{run}} of {{task}}?
message.done: Sent a message to run #{{run}} of {{task}}
message.refused: Message to run #{{run}} of {{task}} · not done
message.effectWaits: Nothing is sent yet. Send message gives the run's agents this message, as the task's composer would: {{text}}
message.effectSent: Sent at {{time}}, as the task's composer sends it; the task's conversation shows it as the Orchestrator's: {{text}}
message.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was sent.

then.followUp: Nothing is sent yet. The run is ready for review: sending follows it up, and a new attempt works on this message: {{text}}
then.continue: Nothing is sent yet. The run failed or waits for a decision: sending continues it with this message's instructions: {{text}}
then.resume: Nothing is sent yet. A pause stopped the run: sending resumes it, and its agent reads this message: {{text}}
then.continueInterrupted: Nothing is sent yet. The run was interrupted: sending continues it from its last checkpoint, and its agent reads this message: {{text}}
then.raiseLimit: Nothing is sent yet. The run stopped at a limit: the message waits until you raise it on the task's Summary: {{text}}
then.runAgain: Nothing is sent yet. The run ended: sending runs the task again, and its next run's first agent reads this message: {{text}}

message.effectRanAgain: Started run #{{run}} at {{time}}; its first agent reads: {{text}}
message.effectRanAgainUnread: Started the task's next run at {{time}}; its first agent reads: {{text}}

publish.effectWaits: Nothing is published yet. Agents read v{{before}} until you publish v{{version}}; a run already under way keeps the version it started with.
publish.effectWaitsProfile: Nothing is published yet. {{name}} keeps v{{before}} until you publish v{{version}}.
publish.effectFirst: Nothing is published yet. No agent gets {{name}} until you publish v{{version}}.
publish.effectApplied: Agents read v{{version}} from their next step.
publish.effectAppliedKeeping: Agents read v{{version}} from their next step. The {{count}} runs under way keep v{{before}} until they finish.
publish.effectAppliedKeepingOne: Agents read v{{version}} from their next step. The run under way keeps v{{before}} until it finishes.
publish.effectDone: Let the Orchestrator publish drafts is on, so the chat published it without asking. Agents read v{{version}} from their next step.
publish.effectDoneKeeping: Let the Orchestrator publish drafts is on, so the chat published it without asking. Agents read v{{version}} from their next step; runs under way keep v{{before}}.
publish.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was published; the draft stays in {{place}}.
publish.widens: This draft widens what {{name}} may do, so it waits for you even though Let the Orchestrator publish drafts is on. Let automation change agent permissions is off.
publish.widensWaits: This draft widens what {{name}} may do. Check what it widens before you publish it.

cancel.effectWaits: Nothing has stopped yet. Cancel stops the run's agents now; its worktree, branch and finished steps stay so you can read what it did. Nothing is merged or deleted.
cancel.effectApplied: Its agents stopped at {{time}}. The worktree and the branch {{branch}} are kept; {{task}} can run again from Tasks.
cancel.effectAppliedPlain: Its agents stopped at {{time}}. Its worktree and branch are kept; {{task}} can run again from Tasks.
cancel.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. The run goes on.

merge.effectWaitsInto: Nothing is merged yet. Merge into {{into}} merges it as Merge in the task's review does, after the same checks.
merge.effectWaits: Nothing is merged yet. Merge merges it as Merge in the task's review does, after the same checks.
merge.effectOnItsOwn: Merged by the Orchestrator on its own, as you let it merge finished runs: {{into}} moved forward to {{revision}}.
merge.effectOnItsOwnPlain: Merged by the Orchestrator on its own, as you let it merge finished runs.
merge.effectOutside: {{into}} holds this run’s work already: it was merged without Orchester. Nothing is merged again.
merge.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. Nothing was merged; the run stays ready for review.

start.effect: Auto mode is on in {{project}}, so the Orchestrator started this run without asking. It went through the queue's checks, as Start in Tasks does.

facts.diffCut: More of the text changes: open the draft to read all of it.
facts.unreadable: What this card acts on can't be read: {{reason}}
facts.choiceResolve: Ask {{step}}'s agent to resolve the conflicts with {{branch}}
facts.conflictNote: Merge {{branch}} in, resolve the conflicts keeping both sides' intent, and commit the merge.

widens.writableFolder: a writable folder outside the worktree
widens.stepToolCalls: step {{step}} tool calls not asked about

continue.waitsResolve: Send run #{{run}} of {{task}} back to {{step}} to resolve its conflicts with {{branch}}?
continue.doneResolve: Sent run #{{run}} of {{task}} back to {{step}} to resolve its conflicts with {{branch}}
continue.effectWaitsRetry: Nothing changed yet. Allow retry runs the stopped step once more, as the task's Summary does.
continue.effectWaitsReturn: Nothing changed yet. Return sends the work back to {{step}}, with the note for its agent, as the task's Summary does.
continue.effectWaitsResolve: Nothing changed yet. Its agent at {{step}} merges {{branch}} in and resolves the conflicting files, as the task's Ask an agent to resolve does; the steps after it run again.
continue.effectApplied: The run went on at {{time}}, as the task's Summary continues it.
continue.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. The run still waits for your decision on its Summary.
continue.effectDismissedResolve: You dismissed it. The conflicts still wait on the task's Summary.

pause.effectWaits: Nothing changed yet. Pause stops the run at its next checkpoint, as the task's page does.
pause.effectApplied: The run pauses at its next checkpoint; asked at {{time}}.
pause.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. The run goes on.

resume.effectWaits: Nothing changed yet. Resume lets the paused run go on, as the task's page does.
resume.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. The run stays paused.

release.waits: Let the project's new starts go on?
release.waitsGroup: Let new starts of {{group}}'s group go on?
release.effectWaits: Nothing changed yet. Release lets the held tasks start again, in the queue's order.
release.effectDismissed: You dismissed it. New starts stay held.

git.losesOne: Applying it loses the work listed above.
git.losesCount: Applying it loses the {{count}} items listed above.
git.losesNothingRead: git lists nothing this would lose now; it still cannot be undone from here.
git.effectDone: git did it and said nothing more.
git.effectApplied: You applied it: git ran the commands above.

loses.resetHard: Moves the branch back: the commits listed leave it, and uncommitted changes to tracked files are discarded. Nothing has run yet.
loses.reset: Moves the branch back: the commits listed leave it; the files keep their contents. Nothing has run yet.
loses.clean: Deletes the untracked files listed for good: git never had them. Nothing has run yet.
loses.deleteBranch: Deletes the branch: the commits listed are on no other branch and are lost with it. Nothing has run yet.
loses.deleteRemoteBranch: Deletes the remote's branch: the commits listed are on no local branch. Nothing has run yet.
loses.forcePush: Pushes over what the remote holds: the commits listed leave the remote's branch. Only if the remote still holds what this card read. Nothing has run yet.
loses.discardChanges: Discards the uncommitted changes listed, staged and not. Nothing has run yet.
loses.switchDiscarding: Switches branch and discards the uncommitted changes listed. Nothing has run yet.
loses.rebase: Writes the commits listed anew on top of the other branch; a conflict undoes it. Nothing has run yet.
loses.deleteTag: Deletes the tag. Nothing has run yet.
loses.abortMerge: Aborts the merge in progress: the changes listed and every resolution made in it are discarded. Nothing has run yet.

line.limitPlan: Stopped at an account's plan limit
line.interrupted: Interrupted when Orchester or its runner closed
line.limitDailyMore: Stopped at the daily budget · {{count}} more runs
line.limitGroupMore: Stopped at their group's budget · {{count}} more runs

end.effectReadyAnswering: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on, so the Orchestrator tells you it is ready, and merges it only if you asked it to here.
end.effectAnswering: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on, so the Orchestrator reads the run and tells you what happened and the choices you have.
end.effectContinuing: Let the Orchestrator continue interrupted runs is on too, so the Orchestrator continues the run once from its last checkpoint and tells you.
end.effectInterruptedAgain: It was interrupted again within 10 minutes of the time before, so the Orchestrator leaves it to you and tells you what happened and the choices you have.
end.effectMerging: Let the Orchestrator merge finished runs on its own is on too, so the Orchestrator merges the run once and tells you; conflicts it proposes to send back to an agent, anything else it leaves to you.
end.effectMergeLeft: Let the Orchestrator merge finished runs on its own is on, but this run is yours to merge: {{why}}. The Orchestrator tells you it is ready.

mergeLeft.notReady: it is no longer the task's latest run that succeeded
mergeLeft.acceptedByAutomation: its step {{step}} passed only because automation accepted it as it was
mergeLeft.held: new starts are held for its group or the project
mergeLeft.optedOut: the task says Don't merge automatically
mergeLeft.deliveredByQueue: its pipeline ends in a Deliver step, so the merge queue delivers it

end.effectContention: The project database stayed busy for more than 3 runs within 10 minutes, so the Orchestrator continues none of them by itself: it tells you, and running fewer agents at once helps.
end.effectQueued: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on: the Orchestrator reads it after the turn under way ends, while the run still stands so.
end.effectOwn: It followed the Orchestrator's own decision on this run, so it waits for you: the Orchestrator doesn't take it up by itself.
end.effectWaits: It waits for you on the task's Summary. Ask the Orchestrator here to read it with you.

report.title: Daily report · {{day}}
report.effectSummary: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on, so the Orchestrator reads the report and adds a short summary and its recommendations below. It changes nothing: what it recommends is yours to do.
report.effectQueued: Let the Orchestrator answer agents is on: the Orchestrator adds a summary and its recommendations after the turn under way ends.
report.asOf: Runs, waits and the queue as they stood at {{time}}.

none.done: Nothing was merged, and the Orchestrator did nothing itself.
none.stands: No run is ready to merge, stopped or at work.
none.next: No task waits in the queue.

report.mergedByOrchestrator: - Merged by the Orchestrator: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{time}}
report.mergedOnItsOwn: - Merged by the Orchestrator on its own: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{time}}
report.ready: - Ready to merge: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}}; merge it on its Summary

stopped.failed: - Failed: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}}; return it to an earlier step or run it again on its Summary
stopped.retries: - Waits for you: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} used up its retries; allow one more or return it on its Summary
stopped.brokeAgain: - Waits for you: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} broke again; allow a retry or return it on its Summary
stopped.noRoute: - Waits for you: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} reported the work failed with no step to return it to; decide on its Summary
stopped.unverified: - Waits for you: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} could not check everything; accept, retry or return it on its Summary
stopped.unchanged: - Waits for you: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} was not run again on unchanged work; accept, retry or return it on its Summary
stopped.limitTokens: - At a limit: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} used its token budget; raise it on its Summary
stopped.limitTime: - At a limit: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} reached its time limit; raise it on its Summary
stopped.limitDaily: - At a limit: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} stopped at the daily budget; resume it once the day has room, or raise the budget
stopped.limitGroup: - At a limit: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} stopped at its group's budget; raise the group's budget
stopped.limitStep: - At a limit: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} used the step's budget; raise it on its Summary
stopped.limitPlan: - At a limit: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{step}} reached an account's plan limit; resume it once the plan allows
stopped.interrupted: - Interrupted: [{{task}} · {{title}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}}; continue it from its last checkpoint on its Summary

wait.question: - Question: [{{task}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{what}}
wait.message: - Waits for a message: [{{task}}]({{link}}) — run #{{run}} at {{what}}

usage.totalUnlimited: - Tokens: [{{spent}}]({{link}}) — {{time}} of agent time; no daily limit
